newsitem.title: USA: Venezuela to seek 18-month IMF standby program.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to seek 18-month IMF standby program.

text.p: Venezuela will seek an 18-month standby program with the International Monetary Fund to follow an agreement that expires in July, Venezuelan Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said Tuesday.
Matos, who attended the IMF/World Bank spring gathering this week, said he will meet with IMF managing director Michel Camdessus on Wednesday to discuss the new program.
"I'll be talking to Mr. Camdessus tomorrow about the idea of renewing our standby program," Matos told reporters after attending a conference for businessmen.

The Venezuelan government won the IMF's and the World Bank's support last year for its "Agenda Venezuela" stabilization plan, under which it scrapped unsuccessful government price controls and state subsidies.

Thanks to a revenue windfall from rising oil prices which fattened its foreign reserves last year, Venezuela was able to waive the last tranches of the $1.4 billion loan the IMF had granted it in July under the 12-month program.
Venezuela does not need IMF financing now either, but it wants to have the Fund's technical support for a planned series of structural reforms.
